newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Oct 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning.
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's Supreme Court and chief metropolitan magistrate take up separate requests by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao
The Supreme Court to rule on a request that a hearing in

a criminal cheating case, set for Oct 16, should be shifted to a large conference hall from a crowded local court. The magistrate will rule on Rao's request for extension of bail and exemption from appearance in a local court on forgery charges
** Three major political groupings jockey for power after inconclusive results in elections to the provincial assembly in northern Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous and politically important state
** The Reserve Bank Of India (RBI), the central bank, plans to tap commercial market to raise $400 million foreign currency loan, the Economic Times says

** UTI Bank, chiefly promoted by state-run Unit Trust of India, Life Insurance Corporation and General Insurance Corporation, plans to raise equity through book-building process, the Business Standard reports
** India plans to appeal to the World Trade Organisation against the European Union over the imposition of anti-dumping duty on unbleached fabrics, the Observer says
** The Petroleum Ministry plans to scrap the mandatory state participation clause for its next offer inviting private sector bids for exploration acreages, the Business Line reports
** The Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund of Japan will pick up equity in Indian infrastructure projects involving Japanese corporates, the Economic Times says
** The spot dollar/rupee opened steady at 35.63/64 per dollar and seen range-bound, dealers said
MARKETS:
** On Thursday, shares recovered smartly on domestic institutional buying and short covering by local punters, brokers said
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index firmed 88.71 points, or 2.92 percent, to 3,129.69
** The 100-share National index rose 27.77 points, or 2.04 percent, to 1,388.79
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index advanced 23.7 points, 2.7 percent, to 898.42
** The 500-share index added 17.52 points to 604.98
** The Delhi share index gained 13.35 points to 696.97
** The Calcutta index rose 3.69 points to 420.57
** The Madras index rose 34.34 points to 3,183.72
** The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index added 1.29 points, or 2.21 percent, to 59.99 with the premium over the local market at 8.17 percent
